## [BlackRabbit Encodes](https://blackrabbit.si)

BlackRabbit focuses on **mini encodes** made for users who want to save storage space without giving up solid video and audio quality.
Our goal is simple: find the **best available remux source**, preferably with **dual audio** (**Japanese + English**) when possible, and encode it into:
- **Video:** AV1
- **Audio:** Opus

This makes the releases especially useful for people running automated setups such as **Sonarr**, where smaller file sizes can save a lot of storage over time.

## Our Encoding Approach

Our releases are more than a straight AV1 + Opus re-encode. We do not re-time dialogue or cut content, but we **clean up, optimize, and reorganize the tracks** so every release is tidy, consistent, space-efficient, and behaves correctly across devices and media servers.

The core changes are:
- video is encoded to **AV1**
- audio is encoded to **Opus**
- black borders caused by an incorrect source resolution are automatically cropped
- unnecessary, duplicate, and lower-priority tracks are removed
- overall file size is significantly smaller

The result preserves the actual anime content while making the release **smaller, cleaner, and better organized**.

## Video Handling

- **Automatic cropping** — black borders are detected and removed when the source contains unused picture area or an incorrect stored resolution.
- **Content preservation** — cropping removes only black border area; the actual image content is not cut or re-framed.

## Audio Handling

Beyond re-encoding to Opus, we tidy up the audio tracks so they behave predictably:
- **Japanese and English only** — other audio languages are excluded to reduce file size.
- **Smart bitrates** — the Opus bitrate is chosen per channel layout (mono, stereo, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1, all the way up to 7.1.4).
- **Highest layout only** — only the highest available channel layout is kept for each language.
- **Commentary removal** — all audio commentary tracks are excluded.
- **Uncensored preference** — when both censored and uncensored audio tracks are available, the uncensored track is preferred.
- **Logical ordering** — Japanese audio is placed first and English second.
- **Best-source selection** — when equivalent candidates remain, lossless sources are preferred, followed by the highest-bitrate source.
- **Correct flags** — default, original, and audio-description flags are set properly.
- **Sync correction** — any audio delay/offset baked into the source is corrected so tracks stay in sync.
- **Clean track names** — messy or inconsistent track titles are cleared.

## Subtitle Handling

Main dialogue subtitles are normalized for consistent readability while signs, songs, karaoke, and other typesetting remain untouched:
- **Consistent dialogue styling** — main dialogue uses **Noto Sans** for modern-looking anime or **Noto Serif** when an older or more traditional style better matches the show.
- **High visibility** — dialogue is styled at **80 px** with white text, a black outline, and a black shadow.
- **SRT conversion** — all SRT tracks are converted to ASS and receive the same dialogue style.
- **Typesetting preservation** — only the main dialogue style is replaced; signs, songs, karaoke, on-screen text, and other custom styles are preserved.
- **Unused font cleanup** — font attachments that are no longer referenced by any retained subtitle track are removed from the MKV container.
- **Track classification** — every track is identified as **Full**, **Signs & Songs**, **SDH**, **Honorifics**, **Commentary**, or **Storyboards**, including content-based detection for sources with wrong or missing labels.
- **Fansub priority** — fansub subtitle tracks are preferred over original or official tracks when both are available.
- **Uncensored preference** — when both censored and uncensored subtitle tracks are available, the uncensored track is preferred.
- **Text over image** — picture-based subtitles such as PGS are excluded when a text-based subtitle track is available for the same language.
- **Conditional zlib compression** — subtitle tracks are compressed only when zlib reduces their size by at least **10%**; otherwise they remain uncompressed.
- **Clean, consistent names** — e.g. `Full Subtitles`, `Signs & Songs`, and `SDH`, with the source or release group tagged where known.
- **Correct flags** — default, forced, hearing-impaired, commentary, and original flags are set so players automatically pick the intended track.
- **Logical ordering** — English first, Japanese second, and other languages alphabetically after that; full subtitles before signs & songs; text-based before image-based.
- **Deduplication** — redundant subtitle tracks are removed.

## Source Quality

Source quality is very important to us. If a **better remux/source** becomes available later, we may **re-encode the entire season** using that source and increase the **version number**.
If you know of a better source, **please let us know in the comments**.

## Sonarr Compatibility

Compatibility with automated media systems, especially **Sonarr**, is one of our main priorities. Because of that, we try to keep **file names as Sonarr-compatible as possible** to make library management easier and more reliable.

## Our Priority

Our main goal is to provide **mini AV1 encodes for as many anime as possible** while still maintaining **good video and audio quality**.
When strong AV1 releases from other groups are already available, we would generally recommend using those instead. BlackRabbit's focus is on helping fill the gaps by providing compact, high-quality AV1 encodes across a wide range of titles.

## Optional Support

If you would like to support and help us continue releasing mini AV1 encodes, donations are appreciated but never expected.
